title: Atomic Flag Switch
goal: Set a boolean flag and retrieve the previous state in one atomic step.
hints: Look for a method that unconditionally stores a new value and returns the old value.
The lock is acquired when the previous state was false.
explanation: `swap` sets the new value and returns the previous boolean value in a single atomic instruction. If `previous` was `false`, the caller successfully acquired the lock, so `!previous` evaluates to `true`. `store` returns unit `()`, which causes type error `E0600` when applying the logical NOT `!` operator. `compare_exchange` requires 4 arguments and fails to compile with `E0061` when called with 2 arguments. Returning `previous` directly inverted the boolean condition, making the test fail.
